_comment: JSON has no comment syntax, so this key carries the header the HTML fixtures put in a comment;
parseBoard reads only `jobs`, so it is inert.
CUT: data_compliance, metadata, departments, requisition_id, language, internal_job_id, the ai_*
keys, and all but a few hundred bytes of each `content`. KEPT VERBATIM: id, title, absolute_url,
location, offices, first_published, updated_at, and the exact HTML-escaping of `content`.
ADVERSARIAL CASES, in order: (1) a normal Zurich posting whose bare location.name disagrees with
its fully-addressed offices entry; (2) a non-CH posting that must be excluded; (3) a remote
posting with NO offices whose Swiss-ness exists only inside a multi-country location string —
the row that is lost if only offices are read; (4) a posting with null location and no offices,
which must be dropped rather than guessed; (5) a CH posting with first_published null, so
postedAt must fall back to updated_at; (6) a CH posting missing absolute_url, which must be
skipped without throwing; (7) a Lisbon posting at an employer whose office list includes Zurich,
which must be EXCLUDED — offices are the company's, not the job's, and OR-ing them admitted 15
of 187 rows wrongly on the first live run; (8) a posting with no location.name at all, where the
Swiss office is the only evidence there is and therefore does decide. 'Sion' also appears inside
'Mission' in case 2's title to catch a word-boundary regression.
